correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the general finite connected simple graph argument. Each v contributes A_v=boundary of the simplex on incident edges S_v, a sphere of dimension deg(v)-2; any whole S_v cannot be an open-neighborhood face under girth≥5 and deg≥3. Different star boundaries intersect at a single original edge-vertex when endpoints adjacent, otherwise not, so their point-glued graph of spaces is a wedge of b=m−n+1 loops and all local spheres. For each original e=uv, the extra maximal open-neighborhood simplex B_e on (S_u−{e})∪(S_v−{e}) meets A along two disjoint contractible simplices: the girth hypothesis prevents crossed witnesses. Distinct B_e intersections lie in A because two shared connectors between disjoint edges force a triangle or quadrilateral; each B_e thus contributes exactly one additional circle by homotopy pushout along two contractible components. The total is m+b loops and all local deg−2 spheres, including bridge cases and no regularity assumption. Local boundaries give canonical integral higher homology orientations under automorphisms (not a full equivariant wedge). Inspected exact projective-plane/Petersen/bridge finite verifier and verified closed formulas q2=43 circles and q3=79 circles+26 S2. The all-graph proof rests on these explicit intersection lemmas, not on finite rank logs.
residual_risks: Claim limited to girth≥5 and min-degree≥3; no weakening to triangles/4-cycles/low degrees.
